sections.h2: How do you sell a house fast in Union, NJ?
sections.html:
The quickest sale in Union is a cash purchase from a buyer who takes the house as it is and orders the township's resale inspection. A listing suits a well kept house in a sought-after pocket, and selling without an agent is permitted, but a resale certificate is part of every route.

Union here means Union Township in Union County, not Union City in Hudson County. The Census Bureau estimates 63,675 residents on July 1, 2025, up 6.6% from the 2020 estimates base of 59,733 and up from 56,642 at the 2010 Census. The township covers 9.05 square miles of land, a 2020 density of 6,599 people per square mile.

sections.h2: What is Union Township like, and where are its neighborhoods?
sections.html:
The township sits on the northern edge of Union County and borders eight municipalities: Hillside, Elizabeth, Roselle Park, Kenilworth and Springfield Township, plus Maplewood, Irvington and Millburn across the Essex County line. It was once called Connecticut Farms, was settled in 1667, and was incorporated as a township on November 23, 1808. It became part of Union County in 1857. The Battle of Connecticut Farms was fought here in June 1780.

Residents describe their location by neighborhood more than by the township name, and each pocket has its own character.

  • Five Points, around the junction of Galloping Hill Road, Chestnut Street and Salem Road.
  • Union Center, near Morris and Stuyvesant Avenues.
  • Vauxhall, north of Interstate 78, with its own ZIP code, 07088.
  • Putnam Manor and Putnam Ridge, an older residential section off Colonial Avenue and Morris Avenue.
  • Battle Hill, in the west near the Rahway River and Route 22, and Larchmont Estates by the Larchmont Reservation.
  • Green Lane, a newer community between Kean University and Union Station.

sections.h2: What do Union homes cost, and who owns them?
sections.html:
Census data for 2020 to 2024 give a median owner-occupied value of $451,300 in Union, with 71.5% of the 21,374 households owning their home. Median gross rent is $2,064. Median household income is $119,464, 40.8% of adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher, and 6.7% of residents live in poverty.

Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $3,015, and owners without one report $1,292. Those figures describe a township of owner-occupants, which means most sellers are individuals selling a home they lived in, often an older house that needs updating before a traditional buyer will bid. About 37.1% of residents were born outside the United States, and 48.1% of residents age five and over speak a language other than English at home.

sections.h2: What must a Union seller do before closing?
sections.html:
Union requires a Residential Resale Certificate, also called a certificate of continued occupancy, before a sale. The township's procedure sheet says requests must be made at least ten business days before the inspection date, and the inspection is paid for in advance. The purpose of the visit is to verify smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and fire extinguishers, and every open permit must be closed with the proper inspections first.

Inspections run between 10:00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, and the owner or a representative must be at the house during those hours or a second visit is scheduled at an added charge. The certificate is issued two full business days after final approval and stays valid for three months unless occupancy or ownership changes. It is not transferable.

sections.h2: What does a Union resale inspection look for?
sections.html:
The township's checklist is short and concrete, so a seller can prepare in a weekend.

  • At least one smoke detector on each level, plus one within 10 feet of each separate sleeping area. Two-family houses also need one at the top of each common stairwell.
  • Carbon monoxide alarms outside each sleeping area, within 10 feet of the bedroom doors.
  • A fire extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen, no smaller than 2A:10B:C and no larger than 10 pounds, mounted no more than five feet off the floor and in plain view.
  • Smoke alarms and extinguisher installed with brackets, not double-sided tape.
  • Existing hardwired detection systems from a newer build or renovation kept working, since battery units are not accepted as replacements.

Test every alarm before the inspector arrives. A failed visit means another $80 and another wait, and a cash buyer will often fix these small items before closing so the certificate can issue.

sections.h2: How does Union bill property taxes?
sections.html:
Union property taxes are due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, with a 10-day grace period. The state does not accept postmarks as proof of payment, so a payment must be physically in the Tax Office by 4:30 p.m. to be credited that day. A drop box at the front door of the municipal building on Morris Avenue works around the clock, and cash should never go in it.

The Tax Office collects municipal, county and school taxes and sewer utility bills. Bills equal assessed value times the tax rate, and the Union County Board of Taxation certifies the rate. The collector cannot lower a tax or waive interest. Ask the Tax Office for the quarter-by-quarter status before closing so the title company can prorate correctly. For relief programs, the township's tax page links to a property tax relief page.

sections.h2: How do roads, rail and Kean University affect Union buyers?
sections.html:
Union has about 145.85 miles of roads, crossed by the Garden State Parkway, Interstate 78, U.S. Route 22 and Route 82 on Morris Avenue. Parkway interchanges 139A, 139B, 140, 140A and 141 serve the township. The Union station on NJ Transit's Raritan Valley Line runs to Newark Penn Station, and its lot holds over 450 cars. Bus routes 113, 114 and 117 go to the Port Authority Bus Terminal in Midtown Manhattan, and Newark Liberty International Airport is about six miles east.

Kean University moved to the township in 1958 and serves almost 16,000 students. The Union Public School District runs six PreK-4 elementary schools, Jefferson School for fifth grade, Burnet and Kawameeh middle schools, and Union High School, which enrolled 2,270 students in 2021-22. Retail is a major local strength: the Census Bureau reports 2022 retail sales of $2,699,105,000, or $44,579 per resident, driven by the Route 22 corridor.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate to sell a house in Union, NJ?
faqs.a: Yes, the township requires a Residential Resale Certificate of continued occupancy before a sale. The inspection costs $175 and must be requested at least ten business days ahead.

faqs.q: How long does the Union resale certificate last?
faqs.a: It stays valid for three months from issue unless occupancy or ownership changes in the meantime. It cannot be transferred to another property or owner.

faqs.q: What does the Union inspector check?
faqs.a: The visit checks smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and fire extinguishers, and confirms that every open permit has been closed. Test the alarms before the inspector arrives.

faqs.q: What if my Union house fails the resale inspection?
faqs.a: A re-inspection costs $80, and the seller calls the housing inspector for a new appointment instead of reapplying. Fix the listed items first, since each extra visit adds cost and delay.

faqs.q: When are Union, NJ property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, with a 10-day grace period and no credit for postmarks. Payments must be in the Tax Office by 4:30 p.m. to count that day.
